text:
IncidentBot: PAGED: High 5xx/error rate observed for egress traffic from az-8 -> eu-west-1 (services: embeddings-prod, asset-upload). Spike started ~00:04 UTC. Autodetect: unusual ICMPv6 PTB activity, retransmits. Paging net oncall.
Akash: ack, I'm oncall. looking now. Paging @Sylvia (net oncall).
Sylvia: on it. pulling tcpdump from lb-az8-1 and gw-az8-rt1. can you drop any heavy uploads?
Jen: support is getting multiple tickets from acme-corp and beta customers about upload failures and timeouts. they're seeing `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` and stalled multipart uploads.
Sylvia: tcpdump snippet shows lots of "ICMPv6 Packet Too Big" messages, then TCP retransmit/backoff. looks like PMTUD is failing because intermediate device drops ICMPv6-PTB responses. snippet:```
15:02:12.345678 IP6 fe80::1 > 2001:db8::abcd: ICMP6, packet too big, mtu 1280
15:02:12.345689 IP6 2001:db8::abcd > 198.51.100.5: Flags [P.], seq 1234:2345, ack 987, win 65535, length 1111
15:02:12.346000 IP6 2001:db8::abcd > 198.51.100.5: Retransmission
```
Sylvia: looks like there are jumbo frames on host->switch link (9000) but path to eu-west has lower MTU. some routers are silently dropping the ICMPv6-PTB. probable dualstack path where v6 path has different MTU.
Carl: can we MSS-clamp on egress or fall back to IPv4 for affected prefixes? MSS clamp easiest short-term. Also consider marking routes to prefer IPv4 for these customers while we engage provider NOC.
Akash: agree. quick mitigation plan: 1) Apply MSS clamp on az-8 egress LB 2) Add temporary route policy to prefer IPv4 for 2001:db8::/32 destined to eu-west 3) Open cloud provider ticket and request they stop dropping ICMPv6-PTB.
Sylvia: applying MSS clamp via tc on lb-az8-1 now. command:```
# clamp MSS to 1200 on tcp SYNs egress
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1200
# or using tc egress clsact + bpf for per-flow
```
Sylvia: applied. pushing same rule to lb-az8-2 and gw-az8-rt1. rolling through config.
NetBot: Created provider ticket NET-PROV-78901 with cloud NOC, attached pcap and PMTU evidence. ETA 45m.
SupportBot: Notified affected customers (acme-corp, beta group) with temporary workaround: retry with smaller parts, switching to IPv4 endpoint.
Jen: running synthetic uploads to eu-west via az-8 egress: before clamp upload errored at 6s, after clamp upload completes but slightly slower. logs:```
POST /upload -> 200 OK (12s total)
curl -v6 -> TLS handshake, then finish
```
Akash: good. instrumenting dashboards to watch 5xx and retransmit rate. set alert if > 1% error for 15m.
Sylvia: cloud NOC replied: they see ECMP path where one hop strips ICMPv6. they will escalate to transit provider and propose BGP change. Meanwhile they recommend keeping MSS clamp.
Carl: temporary route policy applied to prefer IPv4 for prefix 2001:db8::/32; this caused small spike in latency but reduced errors by 98%.
IncidentBot: Metrics: 5xx rate for embeddings-prod down from 4.8% -> 0.1% over 12m post-mitigation. retransmit rate down 90%.
Jen: Support confirms customer uploads are back, close customer-facing alerts after 30m stable.
Akash: preparing handoff to day oncall. monitoring window 2h. owner for postmortem: Sylvia (net team). Please capture root cause, timeline, and follow-ups (provider fix, permanent MTU alignment or ICMP passthrough validation, infra test coverage).
Sylvia: noted. adding postmortem ticket INF-4562 and will coordinate with provider for permanent fix. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Carl: small follow-up: add e2e PMTUD test in canary suite that includes IPv6 jumbo frame path checks.
Akash: assigning action items: Sylvia -> provider follow-up, Carl -> canary tests, Jen -> customer comms summary. handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
